title: What does OracleSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of OracleSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, OracleSet creates or updates a ledger price-oracle publication. [1]

The publisher supplies asset-pair price data and update information under the reference's precision and size rules. Ledger inclusion authenticates who published the data, not whether the market price is correct. Consumers need their own source selection and freshness policy. A recorded oracle quote should not be treated as guaranteed executable liquidity. [1]

The OracleSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using OracleSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
